Storage Types and Relational Stores

存储类型与关系型存储

Data storage is an essential component of modern computing systems that plays a vital role in system design. As businesses and organizations grow, they generate and store vast amounts of data, which makes it important to have a scalable, reliable storage infrastructure that can keep up with the increasing demands. Efficient, reliable storage of data is necessary to ensure that applications and services can function effectively and provide optimal performance to end users. Various types of data storage solutions are available, ranging from traditional file-based systems to more modern block and object stores. Databases also play a significant role in storing and managing structured data, making them a critical aspect of system design.

数据存储是现代计算系统的重要组成部分，在系统设计中扮演着关键角色。随着企业和组织的成长，它们产生并存储海量数据，因此拥有一个可扩展、可靠、能够跟上不断增长需求的存储基础设施就变得十分重要。高效、可靠的数据存储是确保应用和服务有效运转、并向终端用户提供最优性能的必要条件。可用的数据存储方案多种多样，从传统的文件系统到更现代的块存储和对象存储都有涉及。数据库在存储和管理结构化数据方面同样扮演重要角色，使其成为系统设计的关键一环。

In this chapter, we will explore different types of data storage solutions in the context of system design. We will start by discussing traditional file-based storage systems and their limitations before moving on to block and object stores, which have become increasingly popular in recent years because they can handle large amounts of unstructured data.

本章将在系统设计的语境下探讨不同类型的数据存储方案。我们先讨论传统的文件存储系统及其局限，然后再转向块存储和对象存储——后者近年来越来越流行，因为它们能够处理大量非结构化数据。

We also cover the different types of relational databases in this chapter. (We will look at nonrelational stores in Chapter 3). As we examine the challenges of scaling relational databases, we’ll cover various techniques, such as indexes, SQL tuning, denormalization, federation, partitioning, sharding, and replication, that can improve performance and meet the demands of large-scale applications.

本章还会讲解不同类型的关系数据库（非关系型存储将在第 3 章讨论）。在考察扩展关系数据库的挑战时，我们会介绍各种技术，例如索引、SQL 调优、反规范化、联邦、分区、分片和复制，它们都能提升性能并满足大规模应用的需求。

By the end of this chapter, you will have a solid understanding of the available data storage solutions as well as the strengths and weaknesses of different relational database types and how they can be used to design efficient, reliable, and scalable systems. This chapter will serve as the foundation for the concepts we’ll use to compare and select AWS relational database offerings, including flavors of Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS) and Amazon Aurora, which are covered in Chapter 10.

学完本章，你将对可用的数据存储方案、以及不同关系数据库类型的优缺点有扎实的理解，并知道如何用它们设计高效、可靠、可扩展的系统。本章将作为后续概念的基础，我们将用这些概念来比较和选择 AWS 上的关系数据库产品——包括 Amazon Relational Database Service（RDS）的各种引擎和 Amazon Aurora，这些会在第 10 章讲解。

Data Storage Format

The evolution of data storage hardware over the years has posed a challenging problem: how to store the data in a particular format that obscures the underlying storage hardware and can be read, written, and modified across different hardware, even as they evolve. This has led computer scientists and engineers to come up with device drivers, specifically storage drivers, which are installed on different OS to enable working with the data on that particular storage hardware; the data is stored in a specific format that is agnostic to the underlying hardware.

多年来数据存储硬件的演进带来了一个棘手的问题：如何把数据以某种特定格式存储起来，既能屏蔽底层存储硬件，又能在不同硬件之间读取、写入和修改，哪怕这些硬件不断演进。这促使计算机科学家和工程师发明了设备驱动程序，具体来说是存储驱动——它们安装在不同的操作系统上，以便在特定存储硬件上处理数据；数据以一种与底层硬件无关的特定格式存储。

Three different formats, shown in Figure 2-1, have emerged based on how the data is logically arranged on the storage hardware: file-based, block-based, and object-based. Each has its own capabilities and limitations. File-based storage organizes and represents the data as a hierarchy of files and folders. Block-based storage chunks data into arbitrarily organized, fixed-size blocks. And object-based storage organizes data as objects linked with the associated metadata. Let’s go through each of these storage formats in detail.

根据数据在存储硬件上逻辑排列方式的不同，出现了三种格式（如图 2-1 所示）：文件式、块式和对象式。每种都有自己的能力与局限。文件式存储把数据组织并表示为文件和文件夹的层级结构。块式存储把数据切分为组织方式任意、固定大小的块。对象式存储则把数据组织为与相关元数据关联的对象。下面我们逐一详细讨论这些存储格式。

File-Based Storage

File-based storage refers to the storage of data in a folder, just like how paper documents are kept in a filing cabinet. When the data is needed, the computer must know the path to find it, which can be a long, arduous path string. File-based storage

文件式存储指把数据存储在文件夹中，就像纸质文件被放在文件柜里一样。当需要数据时，计算机必须知道找到它的路径，而这个路径可能是一长串冗长的字符串。文件式存储

Page 58

is commonly used for storing structured data, such as documents, images, videos, and audio files.

通常用于存储结构化数据，例如文档、图片、视频和音频文件。

Data in files is organized and retrieved using metadata, like in a library card catalog. Imagine a closet full of file cabinets. Every document is arranged in some form of logical hierarchy: by cabinet, by drawer, by folder, by file, and then by paper. The filesystem provides a similar hierarchical structure to organize electronic files, and data is stored in blocks or pages on disk.

文件中的数据通过元数据来组织和检索，就像图书馆的卡片目录一样。想象一个塞满文件柜的壁橱。每份文件都按某种逻辑层级排列：按柜子、按抽屉、按文件夹、按文件，再按纸张。文件系统提供了类似的层级结构来组织电子文件，而数据则以块或页的形式存储在磁盘上。

This is the oldest and most widely used data storage system for direct and network-attached systems. It’s great for storing complex files and easier to navigate than other formats because of the logical hierarchy. When you access files on your personal computer, you leverage the file storage as when a file store instance is mounted to a computer or virtual machine, it is seen as a local directory.

这是用于直连和网络挂载系统最古老、也是使用最广泛的数据存储系统。它很适合存储复杂文件，而且由于逻辑层级的存在，比其他格式更容易导航。当你在个人电脑上访问文件时，你就在利用文件存储——因为当一个文件存储实例被挂载到一台计算机或虚拟机上时，它就被视为一个本地目录。

The caveat with file-based storage is, just like with your filing cabinet, the virtual drawer can open only so far. File-based storage systems must scale out by adding more systems, rather than scale up by adding more capacity.

文件式存储的注意事项是：就像你的文件柜一样，虚拟抽屉能拉开的程度是有限的。文件式存储系统只能通过增加更多系统来横向扩展（scale out），而不能通过增加容量来纵向扩展（scale up）。

Amazon Elastic File System (EFS) is a scalable, fully managed file storage service offered by AWS that provides shared file storage for Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (EC2) instances, enabling multiple instances to access the same data concurrently, which makes it suitable for applications requiring shared access to files. We will cover it in more detail in Chapter 10.
Amazon Elastic File System（EFS）是 AWS 提供的一种可扩展、全托管的文件存储服务，为 Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud（EC2）实例提供共享文件存储，允许多个实例并发访问同一份数据，因此适合需要共享访问文件的应用。我们将在第 10 章详细讲解。

Block-Based Storage

Block-based storage organizes data into fixed-size blocks or pages, which are stored on disk or flash memory. Each block is assigned a unique address, and data can be read or written to individual blocks. Block-based storage is designed to separate the data from the user’s environment and distribute it across multiple environments that are better suited to serve the data. This means that some block data can be on a Windows environment, some on a Linux environment, and so on. When data is requested, the storage software reassembles the data blocks from these environments and delivers them to the user. Typically used in storage area network (SAN) environments, block-based storage requires a functioning server to operate.

块式存储把数据组织成固定大小的块或页，存储在磁盘或闪存上。每个块被分配一个唯一地址，数据可以按块单独读取或写入。块式存储的设计目的是把数据与用户环境分离，并把数据分发到多个更适合提供数据服务的环境中。这意味着一部分块数据可能在 Windows 环境上，另一部分在 Linux 环境上，等等。当请求数据时，存储软件把来自这些环境的数据块重新组装起来，再交付给用户。块式存储通常用于存储区域网络（SAN）环境，它需要一台正常运转的服务器才能工作。

Unlike file-based storage, block-based storage doesn’t rely on a single path to data, so it can be retrieved quickly. Each block lives on its own and can be partitioned so that it can be accessed in a different OS, which gives the user complete freedom to configure their data. It’s an efficient and reliable way to store data, and it is easy to use and manage. It works well for enterprises that perform big transactions and those that deploy huge databases—meaning the more data you need to store, the better off you’ll be with block-based storage.

与文件式存储不同，块式存储不依赖单一的数据路径，因此检索速度快。每个块独立存在，可以被分区，从而在不同的操作系统中被访问，这给了用户完全自由来配置自己的数据。它是一种高效、可靠的数据存储方式，易于使用和管理。它很适合执行大事务、部署巨型数据库的企业——也就是说，你需要存储的数据越多，用块式存储就越划算。

Page 59

The caveat with block-based storage is that it can be expensive. It has limited capability to handle metadata, which means it needs to be dealt with at the application or database level, adding more complexity for a developer or systems administrator to worry about.

块式存储的注意事项是它可能很贵。它处理元数据的能力有限，这意味着元数据需要在应用层或数据库层处理，从而给开发人员或系统管理员增加了更多要操心的复杂度。

Block-based storage is commonly used in enterprise storage systems, such as SAN and network-attached storage (NAS). It provides better performance, reliability, and scalability than file-based storage because each block can act as an independent disk, giving administrators flexibility to configure and allocate storage volumes as needed. This makes block-based storage ideal for large, dynamic enterprise environments, where storage needs to grow or be reconfigured on demand.

块式存储常用于企业存储系统，例如 SAN 和网络附加存储（NAS）。它比文件式存储提供更好的性能、可靠性和可扩展性，因为每个块都可以充当一块独立磁盘，让管理员能按需灵活配置和分配存储卷。这使得块式存储非常适合大型、动态的企业环境——在这些环境中存储需要按需增长或重新配置。

Amazon Elastic Block Store (EBS) offers scalable block storage volumes on the AWS cloud that can be attached to EC2 instances, providing durable, high-performance storage for applications that require low-latency access to data, such as databases and applications that need block-level storage. We’ll cover it in Chapter 10.
Amazon Elastic Block Store（EBS）在 AWS 云上提供可扩展的块存储卷，可以挂载到 EC2 实例上，为需要低延迟访问数据的应用（例如数据库和需要块级存储的应用）提供持久、高性能的存储。我们将在第 10 章讲解。

Object-Based Storage

Object-based storage is a type of storage architecture where unstructured data is broken down into discrete units called objects and kept in a single repository, rather than in traditional file and folder structures or server blocks. These objects are stored across distributed hardware and are accessed using a unique identifier and metadata that describes the data, including information such as age, security and access contingencies, and even details like the location of equipment used to create a video file.

对象式存储是一种存储架构，它把非结构化数据拆分成被称为对象的离散单元，保存在单一仓库中，而不是放在传统的文件文件夹结构或服务器块里。这些对象跨分布式硬件存储，通过一个唯一标识符和描述数据的元数据来访问；元数据包括诸如数据年代、安全与访问约束等信息，甚至包括创建某个视频文件所用设备位置这类细节。

Object storage volumes function as modular units, with each one being a self-contained repository of data. Retrieval of this data is done using the unique identifier and metadata, which distributes the workload and enables administrators to apply policies for more efficient searches. Object-based storage is also known for its scalability, cost efficiency, and suitability for static and unstructured data. It has a simple HTTP API that is used by most clients in all programming languages.

对象存储卷以模块化单元的方式运作，每一个都是自包含的数据仓库。数据的检索通过唯一标识符和元数据完成，这会分散工作负载，并让管理员能够施加策略以实现更高效的搜索。对象式存储还以其可扩展性、成本效益以及对静态和非结构化数据的适用性而著称。它有一个简单的 HTTP API，各种编程语言的大多数客户端都在使用。

However, there are limitations to object-based storage. Objects cannot be modified, meaning that data must be written entirely at once. Also, object-based storage does not work well with traditional databases because writing objects is a slow process, and programming an app to use an object storage API is not as straightforward as using file-based storage.

然而，对象式存储也有局限。对象不能被修改，这意味着数据必须一次性整体写入。此外，对象式存储与传统数据库配合不佳，因为写入对象是一个缓慢的过程，而且编程让应用使用对象存储 API 也不像使用文件式存储那样直接。

Choosing a data storage format depends on the type of data being stored as well as the performance, reliability, and scalability requirements of the system. File-based storage is best suited for structured data while block-based and object-based storage are more appropriate for unstructured data. Block-based storage provides better

选择哪种数据存储格式，取决于所存储数据的类型，以及系统在性能、可靠性和可扩展性上的需求。文件式存储最适合结构化数据，而块式和对象式存储更适合非结构化数据。块式存储提供更好的

Page 60

performance and reliability than file-based storage while object-based storage offers better scalability and cost-effectiveness.

性能和可靠性，而对象式存储则提供更好的可扩展性和成本效益。

Amazon Simple Storage Service (S3) is an object storage service offered by AWS that provides highly scalable and durable storage for a wide range of data types, accessible via APIs. It is suitable for storing and retrieving large amounts of data, backups, and static website content as well as a data lake for analytics. See Chapter 10 for more detail.
Amazon Simple Storage Service（S3）是 AWS 提供的对象存储服务，为各种数据类型提供高度可扩展、持久的存储，并可通过 API 访问。它适合存储和检索大量数据、备份、静态网站内容，也适合用作分析用的数据湖。详见第 10 章。

We have looked at different data storage formats and compared them in terms of usage, cost, performance, and scalability. Next, let’s discuss how data is stored and structured in databases for easy retrieval and processing.

我们已经考察了不同的数据存储格式，并从用途、成本、性能和可扩展性方面对它们做了比较。接下来，讨论数据在数据库中是如何存储和结构化的，以便于检索和处理。

Relational Databases

A database is a structured collection of data that is organized and stored in a computer system for easy access and management. It is designed for efficient storage, retrieval, and manipulation of large volumes of data. A database typically consists of one or more tables, which are organized into rows and columns. Each row represents a unique record in the database and each column represents a specific attribute or piece of information about the record.

数据库是结构化的数据集合，被组织并存储在计算机系统中，以便于访问和管理。它为高效存储、检索和处理大量数据而设计。数据库通常由一个或多个表组成，这些表按行和列组织。每行代表数据库中一条唯一的记录，每列代表该记录的某个特定属性或某条信息。

A database management system (DBMS), on the other hand, is a collection of software systems that sits on top of a database, acting as a bridge between the database and users, as shown in Figure 2-2. A DBMS offers multiple interfaces or APIs that enable users to store, retrieve, and manipulate data. The DBMS also provides a range of features related to transactions, recovery, backups, concurrency, authentication and authorization, metadata catalog, and other capabilities.

而数据库管理系统（DBMS）则是一套软件系统，位于数据库之上，充当数据库与用户之间的桥梁，如图 2-2 所示。DBMS 提供多种接口或 API，使用户能够存储、检索和操作数据。DBMS 还提供一系列与事务、恢复、备份、并发、认证与授权、元数据目录以及其他能力相关的功能。

Page 61

Databases can be classified into two major types based on their structure, usage, and functionality: relational and nonrelational. We’ll go through relational databases in detail in this chapter. We’ll cover nonrelational databases in Chapter 3. Relational databases use a set of tables with relationships between them to organize data. Designed to store and manage large amounts of structured data, relational databases are the most common type of database. They are based on the relational model, which was introduced by Edgar F. Codd in the 1970s. This model organizes data into tables, which can be related to one another using keys. Examples of open source relational databases include MySQL, PostgreSQL, and MariaDB. Oracle, Microsoft SQL Server, IBM Db2, and SAP HANA are preferred as enterprise relational databases.

根据结构、用途和功能，数据库可分为两大类：关系型和非关系型。本章我们将详细讲解关系数据库，非关系数据库在第 3 章讲解。关系数据库使用一组彼此之间存在关系的表来组织数据。关系数据库为存储和管理大量结构化数据而设计，是最常见的数据库类型。它们基于关系模型，该模型由 Edgar F. Codd 于 20 世纪 70 年代提出。这个模型把数据组织成表，表之间可以通过键相互关联。开源关系数据库的例子包括 MySQL、PostgreSQL 和 MariaDB。Oracle、Microsoft SQL Server、IBM Db2 和 SAP HANA 则是企业级关系数据库的首选。

Tables in a relational database are organized into rows and columns, like a spreadsheet. Each row represents a record, and each column represents an attribute or a piece of data about the record. The columns are defined by a data type, which specifies the type of data that can be stored in that column. Figure 2-3 shows a sample implementation of a logical schema design of a database for storing customer orders.

关系数据库中的表按行和列组织，就像电子表格一样。每行代表一条记录，每列代表该记录的一个属性或一条数据。列由数据类型定义，数据类型规定了该列中可以存储何种数据。图 2-3 展示了一个用于存储客户订单的数据库的逻辑 schema 设计示例。

The logical components of a database schema design are:

数据库 schema 设计的逻辑组件包括：

Tables

The fundamental units of a relational database, tables store and organize data in rows and columns. Each table represents a specific entity or concept, and each row in the table represents an individual instance of that entity; each column represents a specific attribute or property.

表是关系数据库的基本单元，以行和列存储并组织数据。每张表代表一个特定的实体或概念，表中的每一行代表该实体的一个个体实例；每一列代表一个特定的属性或性质。

Rows

Rows, also known as records or tuples, represent individual instances of data stored in a table. Each row contains data values that correspond to the attributes defined by the table’s columns. Rows are unique within a table and are typically identified by a primary key.

行，也称为记录或元组，代表存储在表中的个体数据实例。每行包含与表列所定义属性相对应的数据值。行在表内是唯一的，通常由主键标识。

Columns

Columns, also known as fields or attributes, represent the specific properties or characteristics of the data stored in a table. Each column has a defined data type that determines the kind of data it can store, such as integers, strings, dates, or binary data.

列，也称为字段或属性，代表表中所存储数据的特定性质或特征。每列都有一个已定义的数据类型，决定它能存储何种数据，例如整数、字符串、日期或二进制数据。

Relationships

One of the key features of a relational database is the ability to create relationships: associations between tables. This is achieved using keys, which are columns that uniquely identify each record in a table. The most common types of relationships are one-to-one, one-to-many, and many-to-many. These relationships help maintain data consistency and enable efficient retrieval of related information.

关系数据库的关键特性之一是能够创建关系：即表与表之间的关联。这是通过键实现的，键是能唯一标识表中每条记录的列。最常见的关系类型有一对一、一对多和多对多。这些关系有助于维护数据一致性，并能高效检索相关信息。

Page 62

Keys

Keys are used to establish relationships between tables and ensure data integrity. The primary key identifies each row in a table, and it must have a unique value for each record. Foreign keys are used to establish relationships between tables by referencing the primary key of another table. Establishing these relationships between tables using keys enables data to be easily retrieved and updated across multiple tables. We will cover keys in more detail later in this section.

键用于在表之间建立关系并确保数据完整性。主键标识表中的每一行，并且对每条记录必须有一个唯一值。外键通过引用另一张表的主键来在表之间建立关系。用键在表之间建立这些关系，使得跨多张表检索和更新数据变得容易。本节稍后我们会更详细地讨论键。

Page 63

Indexes

Indexes are data structures that enhance the performance of queries by providing quick access to specific data within a table. They are created on one or more columns of a table, allowing faster search and retrieval operations based on the indexed values.

索引是一种数据结构，通过提供对表内特定数据的快速访问来提升查询性能。它们建立在表的一个或多个列上，使得基于被索引值的搜索和检索操作更快。

Constraints

Constraints enforce rules and conditions on the data stored in a database. Common constraints include primary key constraints, foreign key constraints, unique constraints, and check constraints. They ensure data integrity, enforce referential integrity, and prevent the insertion of invalid or inconsistent data.

约束对数据库中存储的数据强制施加规则和条件。常见的约束有主键约束、外键约束、唯一性约束和检查约束。它们确保数据完整性，强制引用完整性，并防止插入无效或不一致的数据。

Views

Views are virtual tables derived from the data stored in one or more tables. They are created based on predefined queries and provide a way to present data in a customized or simplified manner without altering the underlying tables. Views can be used for security purposes, for data abstraction, or to simplify complex queries.

视图是从一张或多张表所存储的数据派生出的虚拟表。它们基于预定义查询创建，提供一种以定制化或简化方式呈现数据的途径，而无需改动底层表。视图可用于安全目的、数据抽象，或用于简化复杂查询。

Transactions

Relational databases use transactions to keep their state consistent. In the context of DBMS, a transaction is a logical unit of work that represents a series of operations performed on a database as a single, indivisible unit. These operations may include inserting, updating, or deleting data from one or more tables in the database. Transactions ensure data consistency and integrity by allowing multiple operations to be executed together. The ACID (atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability) properties govern the behavior of transactions, which we will cover in more detail later in this section.

关系数据库使用事务来保持其状态一致。在 DBMS 的语境下，事务是一个逻辑工作单元，代表对数据库执行的一系列操作，这些操作被当作单个、不可分割的单元。这些操作可能包括从数据库的一张或多张表中插入、更新或删除数据。事务通过允许多个操作一起执行来确保数据一致性和完整性。ACID（原子性、一致性、隔离性、持久性）性质支配着事务的行为，本节稍后我们会更详细地讲解。

These logical core components work together to form the foundation of a relational database schema, providing a flexible and efficient way to store, organize, and retrieve structured data.

这些逻辑核心组件协同工作，共同构成关系数据库 schema 的基础，提供一种灵活而高效的方式来存储、组织和检索结构化数据。

Relational Database Concepts

Now let’s look at the basic concepts, including structured query language (SQL), ACID, and the entity-relationship (ER) model, that form the foundations of modern relational databases.

现在我们来看看构成现代关系数据库基础的几个基本概念，包括结构化查询语言（SQL）、ACID 和实体-关系（ER）模型。

SQL

Relational databases use SQL to manipulate and retrieve data. SQL allows users to create, modify, and query databases with a set of commands. Some common SQL commands include SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE. The query language serves as a programming language that establishes the syntax, structure, and semantics

关系数据库使用 SQL 来操作和检索数据。SQL 让用户能用一组命令创建、修改和查询数据库。一些常见的 SQL 命令包括 SELECT、INSERT、UPDATE 和 DELETE。这种查询语言充当一种编程语言，确立了与数据库交互的语法、结构和语义

Page 64

governing interactions with the database. It provides a standardized way to store, access, and manipulate data within the database.

规范。它提供了一种标准化的方式，在数据库内存储、访问和操作数据。

SQL can be categorized into these four types, each serving a distinct purpose:

SQL 可分为以下四类，每类服务于不同目的：

Data definition language (DDL)

DDL is a query language used to create and modify the structure and framework of database objects. It encompasses operations like creating tables, defining indexes, dropping tables, and removing indexes.

DDL（数据定义语言）是一种用于创建和修改数据库对象结构与框架的查询语言。它涵盖创建表、定义索引、删除表和移除索引等操作。

Data manipulation language (DML)

DML is a query language employed to create, update, delete, and retrieve information from the database. It involves operations like inserting rows into tables, updating existing rows, deleting rows, and querying data.

DML（数据操纵语言）是一种用于在数据库中创建、更新、删除和检索信息的查询语言。它涉及向表中插入行、更新已有行、删除行以及查询数据等操作。

Data control language (DCL)

DCL is a query language designed to grant or revoke access to entities and operations within the database for clients. It includes commands like granting privileges to users, revoking privileges, and managing security permissions.

DCL（数据控制语言）是一种为客户端授予或撤销对数据库内实体和操作访问权限而设计的查询语言。它包括向用户授予权限、撤销权限以及管理安全权限等命令。

Transaction control language (TCL)

TCL is a query language dedicated to managing and ensuring the consistent execution of a group of database operations as a single unit. It encompasses commands like committing transactions to make changes permanent or rolling back transactions to discard changes.

TCL（事务控制语言）是一种专门用于管理并确保一组数据库操作作为单个单元一致执行的查询语言。它包括提交事务以使更改永久生效、或回滚事务以放弃更改等命令。

Collectively, these query languages form the set of SQL query types, providing the necessary tools to define, manipulate, control access to, and manage transactions within a database system.

这些查询语言共同构成了 SQL 查询类型的集合，提供了在数据库系统内定义、操纵、控制访问以及管理事务所需的工具。

ACID

The ACID model is a set of properties ensuring that database transactions are processed reliably and accurately. ACID stands for:

ACID 模型是一组性质，确保数据库事务被可靠、准确地处理。ACID 代表：

Atomicity

A transaction must be all or nothing. Atomicity ensures that a sequence of operations is treated as a single logical unit of work. Either all the operations within the unit of work are successfully completed or none of them are applied at all. This guarantee prevents partial updates to the database. When all operations are successfully executed, it is known as a commit. In case of failure, all the operations are rolled back, reverting the database to its original state. Atomicity provides application developers with the confidence that the database will always be in a consistent state, even in the event of failures. It also enables safe retrying of operations without concerns about creating duplicate data.

事务必须是全做或全不做。原子性确保一系列操作被当作单个逻辑工作单元处理。要么该工作单元内的所有操作都成功完成，要么一个都不应用。这一保证防止对数据库的部分更新。当所有操作都成功执行时，称为提交（commit）。一旦失败，所有操作都回滚，把数据库恢复到原始状态。原子性让应用开发者放心：即使发生故障，数据库也始终处于一致状态。它还能安全地重试操作，而不必担心产生重复数据。

Page 65

Consistency

A transaction must maintain the consistency of the database. Consistency guarantees ensure that the database transitions from one valid state to another. During the transition, the database enforces rules and constraints defined by the application to maintain data integrity. Consistency is a user-controlled property, meaning that the application must define the valid rules and constraints that lead to a consistent final state. For example, an application may define a rule that the balance of a bank account should always remain positive. The database itself does not enforce these rules but ensures that any changes made to the data adhere to the defined consistency constraints.

事务必须保持数据库的一致性。一致性保证确保数据库从一个有效状态转移到另一个有效状态。在转移过程中，数据库强制执行应用所定义的规则和约束，以维护数据完整性。一致性是一种由用户控制的性质，意味着应用必须定义能导向一致最终状态的有效规则和约束。例如，应用可以定义一条规则：银行账户余额必须始终为正。数据库本身并不强制执行这些规则，但会确保对数据所做的任何更改都遵守已定义的一致性约束。

Isolation

Transactions must be isolated from one another to ensure that they do not interfere with one another. Isolation ensures that concurrent transactions do not interfere with one another, maintaining data integrity and preventing conflicts. Multiple transactions can run simultaneously, and the isolation guarantee dictates how they should interact. If the result of concurrently executing transactions is the same as if they were executed sequentially, then the database supports isolation. Isolation levels, such as Read Uncommitted, Read Committed, Repeatable Read, and Serializable, define the degree of isolation provided by the database. Each level offers different trade-offs between concurrency and data integrity, so the appropriate level should be chosen based on the application’s requirements.

事务之间必须相互隔离，以确保它们不会相互干扰。隔离性确保并发事务互不干扰，维护数据完整性并防止冲突。多个事务可以同时运行，而隔离保证规定它们应如何交互。如果并发执行事务的结果与顺序执行时相同，那么数据库就支持隔离。隔离级别（如读未提交、读已提交、可重复读、可串行化）定义了数据库提供的隔离程度。每个级别在并发度与数据完整性之间提供不同的取舍，因此应根据应用需求选择合适的级别。

Durability

Once a transaction is committed, its changes must be permanent and survive any subsequent failures. Durability guarantees that once a transaction is committed, its changes are permanently stored and will survive system failures, such as crashes or power outages. Typically, this involves persisting the data to nonvolatile storage like a disk. Durability ensures that critical data remains safe and accessible in the long term. Even in the face of catastrophic events, the database will retain the committed changes and recover them when the system is restored.

事务一旦提交，其更改必须是永久的，并能在任何后续故障中存活。持久性保证：事务一旦提交，其更改就被永久存储，并能在崩溃或断电等系统故障中存活。通常这涉及把数据持久化到磁盘等非易失性存储。持久性确保关键数据长期安全、可访问。即使面对灾难性事件，数据库也会保留已提交的更改，并在系统恢复时把它们恢复回来。

The ACID properties ensure that database transactions are processed in a reliable and consistent manner, even when there are failures or concurrent operations. By enforcing these properties, the DBMS can maintain the integrity and reliability of the data stored in the database.

ACID 性质确保数据库事务即使在出现故障或并发操作时也能以可靠、一致的方式被处理。通过强制执行这些性质，DBMS 可以维护数据库中所存数据的完整性和可靠性。

Page 66

ER model

The ER model is a conceptual model used in relational database design to describe the relationships between entities (objects or concepts) and their attributes. It provides a graphical representation of the database schema, which can be used to design, communicate, and understand the structure of the database.

ER 模型是关系数据库设计中使用的一种概念模型，用于描述实体（对象或概念）及其属性之间的关系。它提供数据库 schema 的图形化表示，可用于设计、交流和理解数据库的结构。

The ER model, shown in Figure 2-4, represents entities as rectangles, attributes as ovals, and relationships between entities as diamonds. Relationships can be one-to-one, one-to-many, or many-to-many. The ER model is a useful tool for designing and communicating the structure of a database because it enables designers to visualize the relationships between entities and the attributes that describe them.

ER 模型如图 2-4 所示，它用矩形表示实体，用椭圆表示属性，用菱形表示实体之间的关系。关系可以是一对一、一对多或多对多。ER 模型是设计和传达数据库结构的有用工具，因为它让设计者能够把实体之间的关系以及描述它们的属性可视化。

Schema normalization

Schema normalization is the process of organizing data in a database to reduce redundancy and improve data integrity. It involves breaking down a large table into smaller, more manageable tables, each with its own unique purpose and set of attributes. The goal of schema normalization is to minimize data duplication and ensure that each piece of data is stored in only one place in the database.

Schema 规范化是在数据库中组织数据以减少冗余、提升数据完整性的过程。它把一张大表拆分成更小、更易管理的表，每张表有自己独特的用途和属性集合。Schema 规范化的目标是最大限度减少数据重复，确保每条数据在数据库中只存放在一个地方。

Let’s take an example of a table called Customers in our Orders database that has the following columns: customer_id, customer_name, customer_email, customer_address, and customer_phone. In this table, the customer_name, customer_email, customer_address, and customer_phone are repeated for each customer.

以我们订单数据库中一张名为 Customers 的表为例，它有以下列：customer_id、customer_name、customer_email、customer_address 和 customer_phone。在这张表里，customer_name、customer_email、customer_address 和 customer_phone 会为每位客户重复出现。

To normalize this schema, as shown in Figure 2-5, we can decompose the Customers table into two tables: CustomerInfo and CustomerContact. The CustomerInfo table will contain customer_id and customer_name, while the CustomerContact table will contain customer_id, customer_email, customer_address, and customer_phone.

要规范化这个 schema，如图 2-5 所示，我们可以把 Customers 表分解成两张表：CustomerInfo 和 CustomerContact。CustomerInfo 表包含 customer_id 和 customer_name，而 CustomerContact 表包含 customer_id、customer_email、customer_address 和 customer_phone。

Page 67

By doing this, we have eliminated the redundancy of customer information in the Customers table and stored it only once in the CustomerInfo table. This normalization reduces the storage space required for the database, eliminates data inconsistencies that may arise from redundant data, and makes it easier to update customer information without having to change it in multiple places.

这样做，我们消除了 Customers 表中客户信息的冗余，只把它在 CustomerInfo 表中存储一次。这种规范化减少了数据库所需的存储空间，消除了冗余数据可能导致的数据不一致，并让更新客户信息变得更容易，而不必在多个地方改动。

Keys

Keys are used in relational databases to establish relationships between tables. A key is a column or set of columns that uniquely identifies each row in a table. There are several types of keys:

关系数据库中使用键来在表之间建立关系。键是一列或一组列，能唯一标识表中的每一行。键有以下几种类型：

Candidate key

A candidate key is a column or set of columns in a table that can uniquely identify each record in that table. It is called a “candidate” key because it is a potential primary-key “candidate” for the table. For example, in a table of customers, the customer_email could be a candidate key because each customer has a unique email address.

候选键是表中的一列或一组列，能够唯一标识该表中的每条记录。它之所以被称为“候选”键，是因为它是该表潜在的主键“候选者”。例如，在一张客户表中，customer_email 可以是候选键，因为每位客户都有唯一的电子邮箱地址。

Primary key

A primary key is a candidate key that has been chosen as the main key for the table. It uniquely identifies each record in the table and is used as a reference by other tables that have relationships with this table. For example, in a table of orders, the order ID could be the primary key.

主键是被选作表的主用键的那个候选键。它唯一标识表中的每条记录，并被与该表有关系的其他表用作引用。例如，在订单表中，订单 ID 可以是主键。

Page 68

Foreign key

A foreign key is a column or set of columns in one table that refers to the primary key of another table. It is used to establish relationships between tables and ensure data integrity. For example, in a table of orders, there could be a foreign key that references the customer ID in the Customers table to link each order to the customer who ordered it.

外键是一张表中的一列或一组列，它引用另一张表的主键。它用于在表之间建立关系并确保数据完整性。例如，在订单表中，可以有一个外键引用 Customers 表中的客户 ID，把每笔订单与下单的客户关联起来。

Now, let’s discuss the core components required for a DBMS architecture. The exact architecture may vary from one implementation to another, but the core components generally remain the same.

现在讨论 DBMS 架构所需的核心组件。具体架构在不同实现之间可能有所不同，但核心组件大体一致。

Relational Database Management System Architecture

The architecture of a relational database management system (RDBMS) is shown in Figure 2-6.

关系数据库管理系统（RDBMS）的架构如图 2-6 所示。

Page 69

Let’s go over the components one by one:

下面我们逐一过一遍这些组件：

Query processor

The query processor translates the user query into an execution format suitable for the underlying execution engine. It has two main submodules: the query parser and the query optimizer:

查询处理器把用户查询翻译成适合底层执行引擎的执行格式。它有两个主要子模块：查询解析器和查询优化器：

  • The query parser parses the query given by the user into an abstract syntax tree (AST), which serves as an intermediate representation of the query for execution. The query parser performs parsing, tokenization, syntax validation, semantic analysis, and tree construction in the process of generating the AST.
    查询解析器把用户给出的查询解析成一棵抽象语法树（AST），作为供执行使用的查询中间表示。在生成 AST 的过程中，查询解析器执行解析、词法切分、语法校验、语义分析和树构造。
  • The query optimizer uses the AST generated by the query parser to generate an optimized plan for executing the user’s query. By considering internal statistics like data cardinality, placement, and costs associated with local and remote execution, the optimizer evaluates multiple execution plans.
    查询优化器利用查询解析器生成的 AST，为执行用户查询生成一个优化后的计划。通过考虑数据基数、数据分布以及本地和远程执行相关成本等内部统计信息，优化器评估多个执行计划。

Execution plan

An execution plan represents a series of steps organized in a directed dependency graph, which must be executed in a specific order to fulfill the user’s query. Leveraging the internal statistics, the query optimizer selects the most cost-effective execution plan among the alternatives. It then forwards the chosen plan to the execution engine for processing.

执行计划表示一系列步骤，这些步骤组织成有向依赖图，必须按特定顺序执行才能完成用户查询。查询优化器利用内部统计信息，在多个备选方案中选择成本最低的执行计划，然后把所选计划转发给执行引擎处理。

Execution engine

The execution engine is responsible for executing the query plan generated by the query optimizer. It interacts with the storage engine to retrieve data; performs any necessary joins, filtering, and sorting operations; and returns the result set to the user. The execution engine is also responsible for orchestrating the execution plan across distributed nodes in a distributed relational database.

执行引擎负责执行查询优化器生成的查询计划。它与存储引擎交互以检索数据；执行必要的连接、过滤和排序操作；并把结果集返回给用户。在分布式关系数据库中，执行引擎还负责跨分布式节点编排执行计划。

Storage engine

The storage engine manages the physical storage and retrieval of data, including access and manipulation of data in the database. It handles tasks such as data page management, file allocation, data compression, and indexing. The storage engine interacts with the execution engine to fetch and store data efficiently.

存储引擎管理数据的物理存储与检索，包括对数据库中数据的访问和操作。它处理数据页管理、文件分配、数据压缩和索引等任务。存储引擎与执行引擎交互，以高效地取数和存数。

Buffer manager

The buffer manager handles the management of data buffers in memory. It controls the movement of data between disk and memory, optimizes disk I/O operations, and ensures that frequently accessed data is kept in memory for faster access. The buffer manager minimizes disk access by caching data pages in memory.

缓冲管理器负责管理内存中的数据缓冲区。它控制数据在磁盘与内存之间的移动，优化磁盘 I/O 操作，并确保频繁访问的数据保留在内存中以加快访问。缓冲管理器通过在内存中缓存数据页来尽量减少磁盘访问。

Page 70

Cache manager

The cache manager handles the management and optimization of data caching. It stores frequently accessed data in memory to improve query performance by reducing disk I/O operations. The cache manager ensures that the most frequently used data is readily available in memory for faster retrieval.

缓存管理器负责管理和优化数据缓存。它把频繁访问的数据存储在内存中，通过减少磁盘 I/O 操作来提升查询性能。缓存管理器确保最常用的数据随时在内存中可用，以便更快检索。

Transaction manager

The transaction manager plays a vital role in coordinating and overseeing operations on the data structures within the storage structures module. Its primary responsibility is to ensure that a sequence of operations either executes successfully as a whole or gets rolled back entirely, leaving no partial updates behind. This crucial guarantee provides end users with the confidence that the database will consistently maintain its integrity before and after executing any database operations. To achieve this, the transaction manager collaborates closely with the concurrency control manager and the recovery manager. By leveraging these components, the transaction manager ensures that the visible data in the database remains consistent and aligns with the expectations of end users.

事务管理器在协调和监督存储结构模块内数据结构上的操作方面起着至关重要的作用。它的首要职责是确保一系列操作要么整体成功执行，要么全部回滚，不留任何部分更新。这一关键保证让终端用户放心：在执行任何数据库操作前后，数据库都会始终保持其完整性。为实现这一点，事务管理器与并发控制管理器和恢复管理器密切协作。借助这些组件，事务管理器确保数据库中可见的数据保持一致，并与终端用户的预期相符。

Concurrency control manager

The concurrency control manager handles concurrent access to the database by multiple users or transactions. It ensures that transactions are executed in an isolated and consistent manner, preventing conflicts and maintaining data integrity. It manages locking, transaction isolation levels, and conflict-resolution mechanisms.

并发控制管理器处理多个用户或事务对数据库的并发访问。它确保事务以隔离、一致的方式执行，防止冲突并维护数据完整性。它管理加锁、事务隔离级别和冲突解决机制。

Recovery manager

The recovery manager ensures the durability and reliability of the database in the event of failures or crashes. It manages transaction logging, checkpointing, and crash-recovery mechanisms to maintain data integrity and consistency. The recovery manager ensures that the database can be restored to a consistent state after a failure.

恢复管理器在发生故障或崩溃时确保数据库的持久性和可靠性。它管理事务日志、检查点和崩溃恢复机制，以维护数据完整性和一致性。恢复管理器确保数据库在故障后能被恢复到一致状态。

The recovery manager ensures durability by maintaining an immutable data structure known as a log file within the DBMS. This log file diligently records every write operation applied to the database to facilitate recovery processes. Essentially, the recovery manager acts as a reliable and persistent intermediate storage for all write requests.

恢复管理器通过在 DBMS 内维护一种被称为日志文件的不可变数据结构来确保持久性。这个日志文件认真记录应用到数据库的每一次写操作，以便于恢复过程。本质上，恢复管理器充当所有写请求的一个可靠、持久的中间存储。

Each written page is meticulously preserved in the primary memory, designated as a “dirty page.” To ensure durability, the recovery manager batches all the dirty pages and asynchronously synchronizes them with the disk. Once the dirty pages have been successfully flushed to disk, they are considered “clean pages.”

每个被写入的页都被精心保存在主存中，标记为“脏页”。为确保持久性，恢复管理器把所有脏页分批，并异步地与磁盘同步。一旦脏页成功冲刷到磁盘，它们就被视为“干净页”。

In addition, before a write request is acknowledged as completed by the client, it is appended to a disk-resident append-only data structure. This step provides a safeguard against data loss of dirty pages in the event of a crash or system restart.

此外，在一个写请求被客户端确认为完成之前，它会被追加到一个驻留磁盘、只追加（append-only）的数据结构中。这一步为崩溃或系统重启时脏页的数据丢失提供了防护。

Page 71

The log file serves as a valuable checkpoint, allowing the recovery process to restore data for the dirty pages. On system restart, the OS flushes all remaining dirty pages to disk and discards any uncommitted transactions. This ensures that the system begins in a clean state, ready to process subsequent writes and reads without the risk of incomplete or inconsistent data.

日志文件充当一个宝贵的检查点，让恢复过程能够恢复脏页的数据。系统重启时，操作系统把所有剩余脏页冲刷到磁盘，并丢弃任何未提交的事务。这确保系统以干净状态启动，准备好处理后续的读写，而没有数据不完整或不一致的风险。

Security manager

The security manager enforces data security and access controls. It authenticates users, manages user permissions and privileges, and ensures data confidentiality, integrity, and availability. The security manager protects the database from unauthorized access and maintains data privacy.

安全管理器强制执行数据安全和访问控制。它对用户进行认证，管理用户权限和特权，并确保数据的机密性、完整性和可用性。安全管理器保护数据库免受未授权访问，并维护数据隐私。

Catalog

The catalog, also known as the data dictionary or metadata repository, stores the metadata about the database schema, tables, columns, indexes, constraints, and other database objects. It provides information about the structure and organization of the database, allowing the RDBMS to interpret and manipulate the data accurately.

目录，也称为数据字典或元数据仓库，存储关于数据库 schema、表、列、索引、约束和其他数据库对象的元数据。它提供关于数据库结构和组织的信息，让 RDBMS 能够准确地解释和操作数据。

These core components work together to provide the necessary functionality for managing and manipulating data in an RDBMS. They ensure efficient query processing, data storage, concurrency control, data recovery, and data security.

这些核心组件协同工作，提供在 RDBMS 中管理和操作数据所需的功能。它们确保高效的查询处理、数据存储、并发控制、数据恢复和数据安全。

In the next section, we will explore the different ways of optimizing query performance in RDBMSs using index types, including primary and secondary indexes, SQL tuning, denormalization, and query federation.

下一节我们将探讨在 RDBMS 中使用各种索引类型（包括主键索引和二级索引）、SQL 调优、反规范化和查询联邦来优化查询性能的不同方式。

Optimizing Relational Databases

Optimizing relational databases is an essential task for any database administrator or developer to improve the performance of the queries that run on top of it. Let’s look at the various ways to optimize databases.

优化关系数据库是任何数据库管理员或开发者的一项基本任务，目的是提升运行在其之上的查询性能。下面我们看看优化数据库的各种方式。

Indexes

One way to optimize SQL queries is by using indexes. An index is a data structure that improves the speed of data retrieval operations on a database table. By creating indexes on frequently used columns, the optimizer can quickly find the data needed to execute the query, resulting in faster query execution times than when performing a full table scan. Columns that you are querying (SELECT, GROUP BY, ORDER BY, JOIN) could be faster with indexes. Indexes are usually represented as self-balancing B-trees that keep data sorted and allow searches, sequential access, insertions, and deletions in logarithmic time. The following are the two types of indexes that can be created in an RDBMS:

优化 SQL 查询的一种方式是使用索引。索引是一种数据结构，能提升数据库表上数据检索操作的速度。通过在频繁使用的列上创建索引，优化器可以快速找到执行查询所需的数据，从而比全表扫描更快地执行查询。你正在查询的列（SELECT、GROUP BY、ORDER BY、JOIN）加上索引后可能会更快。索引通常表示为自平衡 B 树，它保持数据有序，并以对数时间支持搜索、顺序访问、插入和删除。在 RDBMS 中可以创建以下两种索引：

Page 72

Primary indexes

A primary index is an index that is created on a table’s primary key (a column or set of columns that uniquely identifies each row in the table). By creating a primary index on the primary key, the database can quickly find the location of a specific row in the table, resulting in faster retrieval times for the data.

主键索引是建立在表主键（唯一标识表中每一行的一列或一组列）上的索引。通过在主键上创建主键索引，数据库可以快速找到表中特定行的位置，从而更快地检索数据。

Secondary indexes

A secondary index is an index that is created on a nonprimary key column or set of columns. A secondary index can be used to improve the performance of queries that involve filtering or sorting data based on a specific column or set of columns. For example, if a query frequently filters data based on a customer’s phone number, creating a secondary index on the phone number column can significantly improve the query’s performance.

二级索引是建立在非主键列或列组上的索引。二级索引可用于提升那些基于特定列或列组过滤或排序数据的查询性能。例如，如果某个查询频繁按客户电话号码过滤数据，在电话号码列上创建二级索引可以显著提升该查询的性能。

B+ trees are widely used in RDBMSs as an indexing structure for facilitating fast data retrieval and efficient query processing. The B+ tree data structure provides efficient key-based searching and range queries on large amounts of data. A B+ tree is a self-balancing tree data structure that stores data in a sorted manner, as shown in Figure 2-7. It consists of internal nodes and leaf nodes, where leaf nodes contain the actual data records or pointers to the data records. Each node in the B+ tree has a fixed number of keys and pointers. The keys in the internal nodes act as separators, guiding the search process, while the leaf nodes store the data records or pointers to the data records in sorted order.

B+ 树在 RDBMS 中被广泛用作索引结构，以促进快速数据检索和高效查询处理。B+ 树数据结构能在海量数据上提供高效的按键搜索和范围查询。B+ 树是一种自平衡树数据结构，以有序方式存储数据，如图 2-7 所示。它由内部节点和叶子节点组成，叶子节点包含实际的数据记录或指向数据记录的指针。B+ 树中每个节点有固定数量的键和指针。内部节点中的键充当分隔符，引导搜索过程，而叶子节点按有序方式存储数据记录或指向数据记录的指针。

When an index is created on a column, a B+ tree index is constructed where each node in the tree corresponds to a range of values from the indexed column. The leaf nodes of the B+ tree contain the values of the indexed column along with the corresponding pointers to the actual data records. B+ trees can also be used to create multicolumn indexes in RDBMSs. In this case, each node in the B+ tree contains

当在某列上创建索引时，会构建一棵 B+ 树索引，树中每个节点对应被索引列的一个值区间。B+ 树的叶子节点包含被索引列的值以及指向实际数据记录的相应指针。B+ 树也可用于在 RDBMS 中创建多列索引。在这种情况下，B+ 树中的每个节点包含

Page 73

multiple keys, allowing for efficient searching and querying based on multiple columns. Composite and multicolumn indexes are beneficial for queries that involve complex conditions or join operations on multiple columns.

多个键，从而支持基于多列的高效搜索和查询。复合索引和多列索引对于涉及复杂条件或多列连接操作的查询很有帮助。

B+ trees provide efficient key-based searching and range queries, which are crucial for improving query performance in RDBMSs. When a query involves searching for a specific value or a range of values, the B+ tree index allows the database system to navigate the tree quickly to find the desired data records. The balanced nature of the B+ tree ensures that the height of the tree remains relatively small, resulting in faster search operations with logarithmic time complexity.

B+ 树提供高效的按键搜索和范围查询，这对提升 RDBMS 的查询性能至关重要。当查询涉及搜索某个特定值或某个值范围时，B+ 树索引让数据库系统能够快速在树中导航，找到所需的数据记录。B+ 树的平衡性确保树高保持相对较小，从而以对数时间复杂度实现更快的搜索。

B+ trees also enable efficient sequential and range scans in RDBMSs. The leaf nodes of the B+ tree are linked together, allowing for scanning of the entire index or a specific range of values. Sequential or range scans are often performed for queries involving sorting or aggregations or when a subset of data needs to be retrieved based on specific conditions.

B+ 树还支持 RDBMS 中高效的顺序扫描和范围扫描。B+ 树的叶子节点相互链接，允许扫描整个索引或某个特定值范围。顺序或范围扫描常用于涉及排序或聚合的查询，或需要根据特定条件检索数据子集的场景。

Finally, B+ trees efficiently handle update and insert operations in RDBMSs. When a new record is inserted, the B+ tree index is updated in a way that ensures the tree’s balance and sorted order are maintained. Similarly, when a record is updated, the corresponding entry in the B+ tree index is adjusted accordingly. This ability to handle dynamic updates and inserts without significant performance degradation makes B+ trees suitable for transactional systems.

最后，B+ 树能高效处理 RDBMS 中的更新和插入操作。当插入新记录时，B+ 树索引会以保持树的平衡和有序的方式更新。类似地，当记录被更新时，B+ 树索引中相应的条目也会相应调整。这种能够处理动态更新和插入而不显著降低性能的能力，使 B+ 树适合事务型系统。

Using a lot of indexes comes with its own caveats as placing an index can keep the data in memory, requiring more space. Writes could become slower since the index also needs to be updated. When loading large amounts of data, it might be faster to disable indexes, load the data, and then rebuild the indexes.

使用大量索引也有自己的注意事项：建立索引会把数据保留在内存中，需要更多空间。写入可能变慢，因为索引也需要更新。在加载大量数据时，先禁用索引、加载数据、然后重建索引可能会更快。

SQL tuning

As prescribed in the section “Guideline of Performance: Metrics Don’t Lie” on page 32 in Chapter 1, to improve the performance of SQL queries, it is first important to benchmark and profile your queries to uncover bottlenecks. Benchmarking involves simulating high-load and high-throughput situations, while profiling requires measuring the p90 latency of the query and analyzing the slow query log to identify performance issues. Based on these metrics, SQL tuning is improving the performance of SQL queries by removing the bottlenecks and optimizing query plans.

正如第 1 章第 32 页“性能准则：指标不会说谎”一节所指出的，要提升 SQL 查询性能，首先必须对查询做基准测试和剖析以发现瓶颈。基准测试涉及模拟高负载、高吞吐场景，而剖析则要求测量查询的 p90 延迟并分析慢查询日志以识别性能问题。基于这些指标，SQL 调优就是通过消除瓶颈和优化查询计划来提升 SQL 查询性能。

One way to optimize SQL queries is to minimize large write operations because performing operations like writing, modifying, deleting, or importing extensive amounts of data can have a significant impact on the performance of queries. These operations may even result in table blocking when tasks involve updating and manipulating data, adding indexes or check constraints to queries, processing triggers, and similar actions. Moreover, the act of writing a substantial volume of data will inevitably lead to an increase in the size of log files.

优化 SQL 查询的一种方式是尽量减少大批量写操作，因为执行写入、修改、删除或导入海量数据等操作会对查询性能产生显著影响。当任务涉及更新和操作数据、给查询添加索引或检查约束、处理触发器等动作时，这些操作甚至可能导致表阻塞。此外，写入大量数据的行为不可避免地会导致日志文件体积增大。

Page 74

Another technique to optimize SQL performance is to schedule query execution during off-peak hours. This approach is particularly beneficial when dealing with multiple SELECT queries involving large tables or executing complex queries with nested subqueries, looping queries, and the like. When executing resource-intensive queries in a database, the RDBMS applies locks to the tables involved, preventing simultaneous access by different transactions. Consequently, other users are unable to work with those tables, leading to limited access to specific data. Running heavy queries during peak times not only strains the server but also restricts other users’ data access.

另一种优化 SQL 性能的技术是把查询执行安排在非高峰时段。这种做法在处理多个涉及大表的 SELECT 查询、或执行带嵌套子查询、循环查询等复杂查询时尤其有益。在数据库中执行资源密集型查询时，RDBMS 会对涉及的表加锁，阻止不同事务同时访问。因此，其他用户无法使用这些表，导致对特定数据的访问受限。在高峰时段运行重型查询不仅会给服务器带来压力，还会限制其他用户的数据访问。

Adding multiple tables to a query and performing joins can potentially burden the query and lead to performance issues. Moreover, having a large number of tables to retrieve data from may result in an inefficient execution plan. JOIN elimination is one of the many techniques employed to achieve efficient query plans. Dividing a single query into several separate queries that can be joined later can eliminate unnecessary joins, subqueries, and tables. This approach helps streamline the query and enhance its performance by removing redundant and extraneous elements.

给查询添加多张表并执行连接，可能会给查询带来负担并导致性能问题。此外，需要从大量表中检索数据可能导致低效的执行计划。JOIN 消除是实现高效查询计划的众多技术之一。把单个查询拆成若干可在稍后连接的独立查询，可以消除不必要的连接、子查询和表。这种做法通过移除冗余和多余元素来精简查询并提升其性能。

Enhancing RDBMS performance and optimizing SQL queries are critical tasks for both database developers and administrators. They must meticulously evaluate various factors, such as the selection of specific operators, the number of tables involved in a query, the query’s size, its execution plan, statistics, resource allocation, and other performance metrics. These considerations play a pivotal role in determining whether query performance improves or deteriorates. By carefully analyzing and addressing these factors, developers and administrators can effectively tune and improve query performance.

提升 RDBMS 性能和优化 SQL 查询对数据库开发者和管理员都是关键任务。他们必须细致评估各种因素，例如具体运算符的选择、查询涉及的表数量、查询规模、执行计划、统计信息、资源分配以及其他性能指标。这些考虑对查询性能是改善还是恶化起着关键作用。通过仔细分析和处理这些因素，开发者和管理员可以有效地调优并提升查询性能。

Denormalization

In most systems, read operations significantly outnumber write operations by a ratio of 100:1 or even 1,000:1. Performing a complex database join during a read can be resource intensive, particularly due to disk operations.

在大多数系统中，读操作的数量远超写操作，比例可达 100:1 甚至 1000:1。在读操作期间执行复杂的数据库连接可能非常消耗资源，尤其是因为磁盘操作。

Denormalization is the technique aimed at improving read performance, although it may come at the cost of reduced write performance. It involves duplicating data across multiple tables to avoid costly joins. Some RDBMSs offer materialized views, which handle the task of storing redundant information and maintaining consistency among redundant copies.

反规范化是一种旨在提升读性能的技术，尽管它可能以降低写性能为代价。它涉及跨多张表复制数据，以避免代价高昂的连接。一些 RDBMS 提供物化视图，由它们负责存储冗余信息并在冗余副本之间维护一致性。

When data is distributed through methods like federation and sharding, managing joins across different data centers adds further complexity. Denormalization can help alleviate the need for complex joins in such scenarios. However, denormalization has its disadvantages because of data duplication, which can lead to redundancy. Maintaining consistency among redundant copies requires the use of constraints, which further adds complexity to the database design. If multiple tables store redundant

当数据通过联邦和分片等方式分布时，跨不同数据中心管理连接会增加更多复杂度。在这类场景中，反规范化有助于减轻对复杂连接的需求。然而，反规范化也有缺点，因为数据复制会导致冗余。在冗余副本之间维护一致性需要使用约束，这进一步增加了数据库设计的复杂度。如果多张表存储了客户电子邮箱地址的冗余

Page 75

copies of a customer’s email address—for instance, in the Customers and Orders tables—a unique constraint on the email in the Customers table helps prevent duplicate email entries. Additionally, setting a trigger or cascading update constraints can ensure that updates to the email in the Customers table are automatically reflected in the Orders table, preventing inconsistent copies. Therefore, a denormalized database under heavy write load may perform worse than its normalized counterpart.

副本——例如在 Customers 和 Orders 表中——那么在 Customers 表的 email 列上加唯一性约束有助于防止重复的邮箱条目。此外，设置触发器或级联更新约束可以确保 Customers 表中 email 的更新自动反映到 Orders 表中，防止出现不一致的副本。因此，在高写入负载下，反规范化数据库的性能可能不如其规范化的对应物。

Overall, denormalization can provide performance benefits for read-heavy workloads, but it introduces trade-offs in terms of data redundancy and increased complexity in database management.

总体而言，反规范化可以为读多写少的负载带来性能收益，但它在数据冗余和数据库管理复杂度增加方面引入了取舍。

Query federation

Query federation is a technique that involves splitting a large query into smaller queries that can be executed independently on different database servers. This technique requires schema federation—that is, functional partitioning of the database across multiple database servers. Executing smaller queries on different servers can reduce the overall query execution time, resulting in faster query results. Query federation is useful for optimizing queries that involve large amounts of data or complex joins.

查询联邦是一种把大查询拆分成可在不同数据库服务器上独立执行的小查询的技术。这种技术需要 schema 联邦——也就是把数据库按功能分区到多台数据库服务器上。在不同服务器上执行较小的查询可以缩短整体查询执行时间，从而得到更快的查询结果。查询联邦对于优化涉及大量数据或复杂连接的查询很有用。

By using these techniques to optimize relational databases, database administrators can improve performance and provide faster, more efficient access to data. Next, we’ll cover the techniques used to scale relational databases in practice.

通过使用这些技术优化关系数据库，数据库管理员可以提升性能，并提供更快、更高效的数据访问。接下来，我们将讲解实践中用于扩展关系数据库的技术。

Scaling Relational Databases

As businesses grow and their data needs increase, it becomes necessary for them to scale their databases to handle the increased workload. Scaling refers to the process of increasing the capacity of a database to accommodate more data, users, and transactions. Let’s explore scaling relational databases using partitioning, sharding, and replication.

随着企业成长和数据需求增加，它们有必要扩展数据库以应对增长的工作负载。扩展指的是增加数据库容量以容纳更多数据、用户和事务的过程。下面我们探讨用分区、分片和复制来扩展关系数据库。

Partitioning

Partitioning is the process of dividing a large database table into smaller, more manageable parts called partitions. Each record within the database is assigned to a specific partition, ensuring that every record belongs to one and only one partition. Each partition operates as an independent database, capable of executing read and write operations autonomously. As a result, database queries can be directed toward a single partition to focus on specific data or distributed across multiple partitions for broader processing. The client can direct the query either to a specific partition or to a coordinator node, which then forwards the query to the right set of partitions, thus orchestrating the partitions. The two types of partitioning, shown in Figure 2-8, are vertical and horizontal, with two possible approaches to horizontal partitioning.

分区是把一张大的数据库表划分成更小、更易管理的部分（称为分区）的过程。数据库中的每条记录被分配到一个特定分区，确保每条记录属于且仅属于一个分区。每个分区像一个独立数据库一样运作，能够自主执行读写操作。因此，数据库查询可以被导向单个分区以聚焦特定数据，或分发到多个分区以做更广泛的处理。客户端可以把查询直接发到某个特定分区，或发到一个协调者节点，由后者把查询转发到正确的一组分区，从而编排这些分区。如图 2-8 所示，分区有两种类型：纵向和横向，而横向分区又有两种可能的方式。

Page 76

Vertical partitioning involves splitting a table by columns. For example, a customer table might be split into two tables, one containing customer information and another containing customer contact data.

纵向分区是按列拆分一张表。例如，一张客户表可能被拆成两张表，一张包含客户信息，另一张包含客户联系数据。

Horizontal partitioning involves splitting a table by rows. For example, a large customer table might be split into smaller tables, each containing a specific range of customer records based on their last name or zip code. Horizontal partitioning can have two approaches: hash partitioning and range partitioning.

横向分区是按行拆分一张表。例如，一张大的客户表可能被拆成若干小表，每张表根据客户姓氏或邮编包含特定范围的客户记录。横向分区有两种方式：哈希分区和范围分区。

Hash partitioning

The strategy of partitioning by key hash involves generating a hash of the key and evenly distributing it among the partitions. In this strategy, a hash function (such as MD5 or SHA-256) is applied to the input key of the table. The hash ranges are then divided into buckets, with each bucket assigned to a specific partition. It’s important to note that a single host instance can accommodate multiple partitions.

按键哈希分区的策略是对键生成哈希值，并把它均匀分布到各个分区中。在这种策略中，对表的输入键应用一个哈希函数（例如 MD5 或 SHA-256）。然后把哈希范围划分成桶，每个桶分配给一个特定分区。需要注意的是，单个主机实例可以容纳多个分区。

For this strategy to work effectively, the hash function must be deterministic, meaning that the same key should always produce the same hash value and be directed to the same partition. Additionally, each key should resolve to a unique hash value, ensuring a balanced distribution of data across the partitions.

要让这种策略有效工作，哈希函数必须是确定性的，也就是说同一个键应始终产生相同的哈希值并被导向同一个分区。此外，每个键应解析为唯一的哈希值，确保数据在各分区之间均衡分布。

The advantage of hash partitioning is that it eliminates the problems of hot spots and skewed partitions that can occur with range partitioning by using a unique,

哈希分区的优点是，它通过使用一种唯一的、

Page 77

deterministic hashing strategy. However, since the partitioning is on the key’s hash, this strategy can’t do range queries. We need to query all the partitions if we want to fetch a set of keys, making the DBMS do a scatter and gather pattern.

确定性的哈希策略，消除了范围分区可能出现的热点和倾斜分区问题。然而，由于分区是基于键的哈希，这种策略无法做范围查询。如果我们想取一组键，就需要查询所有分区，让 DBMS 执行一种 scatter-and-gather（散布-收集）模式。

Range partitioning

In range partitioning, we partition a continuous range of keys into separate buckets, which are then assigned to specific partitions. It is important to note that a single host instance can accommodate multiple partitions. The key range assigned to each bucket may or may not be continuous, allowing flexibility in the distribution of data.

在范围分区中，我们把一段连续的键范围划分到不同的桶中，再把这些桶分配给特定分区。需要注意的是，单个主机实例可以容纳多个分区。分配给每个桶的键范围可以是连续的，也可以不是，从而在数据分布上具有灵活性。

Within each partition, the keys are stored in a sorted order. This organization of data enables efficient range scan queries because it simplifies the process of retrieving data within specific key ranges. The system can swiftly access and retrieve data that falls within a given range. In the example shown in Figure 2-8, it becomes easy to retrieve all customers having emails starting with P in lexicographic order. Additionally, the range-partitioning strategy is relatively straightforward to implement.

在每个分区内部，按键的有序方式存储数据。这种数据组织方式支持高效的范围扫描查询，因为它简化了在特定键范围内检索数据的过程。系统可以快速访问和检索落在给定范围内的数据。在图 2-8 所示的例子中，按字典序检索所有邮箱以 P 开头的客户就变得很容易。此外，范围分区策略实现起来相对直接。

However, if the access patterns on partitions are uneven or unfair, certain partitions may end up with more data or queries than others, leading to skewed partitions and placing a heavier load on specific partitions, which can potentially cause congestion. Such imbalanced partitions that experience a disproportionately high workload are called hot spots. For example, in Figure 2-8, if a significant majority of customers have emails beginning with A, that can result in the choking of Partition 1 because of the overwhelming amount of data and queries concentrated in that partition.

然而，如果各分区上的访问模式不均匀或不公平，某些分区最终可能比其他分区承载更多数据或查询，导致分区倾斜，并给特定分区带来更重的负载，从而可能引发拥塞。这种承受了过高、不成比例工作负载的不平衡分区被称为热点。例如，在图 2-8 中，如果绝大多数客户的邮箱都以 A 开头，那可能导致分区 1 被压垮，因为海量数据和查询都集中在那个分区。

Partitioning a database offers advantages for large datasets as well as enables high throughput capability. Partitioning enables data to be distributed across multiple machines via sharding, allowing for the handling of datasets that exceed the capacity of a single machine. By spreading the data across multiple partitions, the database can accommodate and manage large-scale data requirements.

对数据库分区不仅对大数据集有好处，还能实现高吞吐能力。分区通过分片让数据分布到多台机器上，从而能够处理超出单机容量的数据集。通过把数据分散到多个分区，数据库可以容纳和管理大规模的数据需求。

With data distributed across multiple partitions, read and write queries can be processed independently by each partition. This parallel processing capability enables the database to handle a higher overall throughput compared to what a single machine can handle. By leveraging the collective power of multiple machines, partitioning enhances the system’s ability to process concurrent queries and transactions efficiently. Thus, partitioning can improve query performance by reducing the amount of data that needs to be scanned to execute a query. This results in faster query response times and better scalability.

数据分布在多个分区后，读查询和写查询可以由每个分区独立处理。这种并行处理能力使数据库能够处理比单台机器更高的总体吞吐量。通过借助多台机器的合力，分区增强了系统高效处理并发查询和事务的能力。因此，分区可以通过减少执行查询所需扫描的数据量来提升查询性能。这带来更快的查询响应时间和更好的可扩展性。

Page 78

Sharding

Sharding is the process of distributing a large database across multiple servers. Each server contains a subset of the data, and queries are distributed across all servers. Sharding is useful for scaling databases that have become too large to be managed on a single server. For example, in a “customers” database, as the number of customers grows, more shards are added to the cluster to accommodate the increasing load. Common approaches to sharding a customer table include using the customer’s last name, initial, or geographic location.

分片是把大型数据库分布到多台服务器上的过程。每台服务器包含数据的一个子集，查询被分发到所有服务器。分片对于扩展那些已经大到无法在单台服务器上管理的数据库很有用。例如，在“customers”数据库中，随着客户数量增长，会向集群添加更多分片以容纳不断增长的负载。对客户表进行分片的常见方式包括按客户姓氏、首字母或地理位置。

There are two types of sharding, as shown in Figure 2-9: vertical and horizontal, with different possible approaches to horizontal partitioning, including hash-based, range-based, and round-robin sharding.

如图 2-9 所示，分片有两种类型：纵向和横向；横向分片又有不同的可能方式，包括基于哈希、基于范围和轮询（round-robin）分片。

Sharding offers similar advantages to federation, including reduced read and write traffic, decreased replication, and improved cache utilization. It also helps reduce the size of indexes, leading to faster query performance. In the event of a shard failure, the other shards remain operational, although implementing replication is crucial to prevent data loss. Sharding eliminates the need for a central master for write serialization, enabling parallel writes and increasing overall throughput.

分片提供与联邦类似的优点，包括减少读写流量、减少复制和提升缓存利用率。它还有助于减小索引体积，从而带来更快的查询性能。万一某个分片发生故障，其他分片仍可继续运作，不过实现复制对于防止数据丢失至关重要。分片消除了用中央主节点做写串行化的需要，从而支持并行写入并提高总体吞吐量。

However, sharding comes with its disadvantages. Application logic needs to be updated to handle shard-specific operations, potentially resulting in complex SQL queries. Data distribution can become unbalanced, particularly if a shard has a subset of power customers, leading to increased load on that particular shard. Rebalancing shards adds complexity, although using a consistent hash-based sharding function can minimize data transfer. Joining data from multiple shards becomes more challenging, and overall, sharding introduces additional hardware requirements and increased system complexity.

然而，分片也有缺点。应用逻辑需要更新以处理分片特定的操作，可能导致复杂的 SQL 查询。数据分布可能变得不平衡，尤其是当某个分片拥有一部分高价值客户时，会导致该分片负载增加。重新平衡分片会增加复杂度，尽管使用基于一致性哈希的分片函数可以尽量减少数据迁移。跨多个分片连接数据变得更具挑战性，而且总体而言，分片引入了额外的硬件需求和更高的系统复杂度。

Page 79
Page 80

Replication

Replication is the process of copying data from one database server to another. Every node that stores a copy of the data is called a replica. Replication is a key feature in distributed databases that offers several advantages in enhancing availability, load distribution, and latency reduction. By maintaining multiple copies of data across different host machines, replication provides the following benefits:

复制是把数据从一台数据库服务器拷贝到另一台的过程。每个存储了一份数据拷贝的节点称为副本（replica）。复制是分布式数据库的一项关键特性，在提升可用性、负载分布和降低延迟方面有诸多优点。通过在不同主机上维护多份数据拷贝，复制带来以下好处：

High availability

Replication ensures high availability by storing copies of data on multiple host machines. In the event of a failure or downtime of one host machine, the database can seamlessly redirect read and write operations to other live machines that hold replicated data. This fault-tolerance mechanism prevents service disruptions and ensures continuous access to data, enhancing the overall availability of the system.

复制通过在多台主机上存储数据副本来确保高可用。万一某台主机发生故障或宕机，数据库可以无缝地把读写操作重定向到其他持有副本数据的存活机器。这种容错机制防止服务中断，确保持续访问数据，从而提升系统的整体可用性。

Load distribution

With replication, the database can distribute read and write queries across multiple host machines. This load-distribution strategy prevents overburdening of individual machines, thereby improving overall system performance and scalability. By spreading the workload, replication enables efficient utilization of computing resources and better handling of concurrent user requests, resulting in enhanced throughput and responsiveness.

通过复制，数据库可以把读查询和写查询分发到多台主机上。这种负载分布策略防止单台机器负担过重，从而提升整体系统性能和可扩展性。通过分散工作负载，复制实现计算资源的高效利用，并更好地处理并发用户请求，从而提高吞吐量和响应能力。

Reduced latency

Replicating data across geographically distributed host machines allows for placing the replicated copies closer to end users. This proximity reduces the network latency experienced by users when accessing the database. By minimizing the distance between the data and the user, replication improves response times and enhances the user experience, especially in scenarios where low latency is critical, such as real-time applications or distributed systems with users located in different regions.

把数据复制到地理上分布的多台主机上，可以让副本更贴近终端用户。这种地理上的邻近性减少了用户访问数据库时的网络延迟。通过缩短数据与用户之间的距离，复制改善了响应时间并提升了用户体验，尤其是在低延迟至关重要的场景中，例如实时应用，或用户分布在不同地区的分布式系统。

Disaster recovery and data resilience

Replication serves as a foundation for disaster-recovery strategies. By maintaining multiple copies of data, distributed databases can withstand catastrophic events, hardware failures, or natural disasters. In case of data loss or unavailability on one host machine, the replicated copies can be used for data recovery and system restoration. Replication ensures data resilience and minimizes the risk of data loss, contributing to the overall reliability and robustness of the database.

复制是灾难恢复策略的基础。通过维护多份数据拷贝，分布式数据库能够承受灾难性事件、硬件故障或自然灾害。万一某台主机上的数据丢失或不可用，副本可用于数据恢复和系统还原。复制确保数据韧性并尽量降低数据丢失风险，从而提升数据库的整体可靠性和健壮性。

Scalability and performance

Replication plays a crucial role in scaling distributed databases. As the data size or user load increases, additional host machines can be added to the system, each hosting a replicated copy of the data. This horizontal-scaling approach allows the

复制在扩展分布式数据库方面起着关键作用。随着数据量或用户负载增加，可以向系统中添加更多主机，每台主机都托管一份数据副本。这种水平扩展方式让

Page 81

database to handle larger workloads and accommodate growing user demands. By distributing data and queries, replication contributes to improved system performance, enabling efficient parallel processing and reducing response times.

数据库能够处理更大的工作负载并满足不断增长的用户需求。通过分布数据和查询，复制有助于提升系统性能，实现高效的并行处理并缩短响应时间。

The two types of replication for RDBMSs are single-leader and multileader, both of which are illustrated in Figure 2-10.

RDBMS 的两种复制类型是单主（single-leader）和多主（multileader），两者如图 2-10 所示。

In single-leader replication, one database server serves as the leader, and the other servers serve as followers. The leader server handles all write operations while the follower servers handle read operations. Changes made to the leader server are replicated to the follower servers, ensuring that all servers contain the same data either synchronously or asynchronously. This type of replication is useful for scaling read-heavy databases.

在单主复制中，一台数据库服务器充当 leader，其他服务器充当 follower。leader 服务器处理所有写操作，而 follower 服务器处理读操作。对 leader 所做的更改被复制到 follower 服务器，确保所有服务器以同步或异步方式持有相同数据。这种复制类型适合扩展读多写少的数据库。

In multileader replication, each database server can both read and write data. Changes made to one server are replicated to the other server either synchronously or asynchronously, ensuring that all servers contain the same data. This type of replication is useful for scaling databases that require high availability. In single-leader, there will be a lag in leader election and promotion, but in multileader, failure will be opaque, leading to a high-availability setup. However, this comes with a trade-off: conflict resolution, which we discussed in Chapter 1. Since writes can occur on multiple leaders independently, conflicting updates may arise when the same data is modified in different locations simultaneously.

在多主复制中，每台数据库服务器都既能读又能写数据。对一台服务器所做的更改以同步或异步方式复制到另一台服务器，确保所有服务器持有相同数据。这种复制类型适合扩展要求高可用的数据库。在单主模式中，选主和提升会有延迟，但在多主模式中，故障是不透明的（对用户无感），从而形成高可用架构。然而这伴随一个取舍：冲突解决，我们在第 1 章讨论过。由于写入可以独立地发生在多个 leader 上，当同一数据在不同位置被同时修改时，就可能出现冲突的更新。

For these replication types, replication can be done on follower nodes as full replication, snapshot-based replication, transactional replication (i.e., replicating the transactional updates), or key-based incremental replication (i.e., scanning the database for modified keys and only replicating data for those keys). The replication can be done either synchronously or asynchronously, each with its own caveats.

对于这些复制类型，在 follower 节点上的复制可以是全量复制、基于快照的复制、事务复制（即复制事务性更新），或基于键的增量复制（即扫描数据库找出被修改的键，只复制这些键的数据）。复制可以同步或异步进行，各有各的注意事项。

Page 82

Synchronous replication

In distributed databases, synchronous replication provides a mechanism for replicating data from a leader replica to follower replicas using synchronous communication, keeping data always up to date across all replicas. By maintaining synchronous replicas that are always in sync with the leader replica, this replication mechanism offers several advantages:

在分布式数据库中，同步复制提供一种机制，通过同步通信把数据从 leader 副本复制到 follower 副本，使所有副本上的数据始终保持最新。通过维护始终与 leader 副本同步的同步副本，这种复制机制提供以下优点：

Consistent writes

With synchronous replication, the client considers a write operation successful only when it is acknowledged by both the leader replica and the synchronous follower replica. This strict synchronization ensures that the data remains consistent across replicas. By waiting for confirmation from both replicas, the system guarantees that the write has been durably committed and is available for subsequent read operations. Though it increases latency, this consistency is vital for applications that require strict data integrity and accuracy.

在同步复制下，客户端只有在写操作同时被 leader 副本和同步 follower 副本确认后，才认为它成功。这种严格同步确保数据在各副本之间保持一致。通过等待两个副本的确认，系统保证写入已被持久提交，并可供后续读操作使用。尽管这会增加延迟，但这种一致性对于要求严格数据完整性和准确性的应用至关重要。

Immediate failover

One significant advantage of synchronous replication is its ability to facilitate immediate failover in the event of a leader-replica crash. Since the synchronous replicas are always up to date with the leader, any of these replicas can be immediately promoted as the new leader without any data loss. This seamless transition ensures continuous availability of the system even when there are failures. By eliminating downtime and minimizing data loss, synchronous replication enhances the overall resilience and reliability of the distributed system.

同步复制的一个显著优点是，它能在 leader 副本崩溃时促成立即故障转移。由于同步副本始终与 leader 保持最新，这些副本中的任何一个都可以被立即提升为新 leader，而不会丢失任何数据。这种无缝过渡确保即使发生故障，系统也持续可用。通过消除停机时间并尽量减少数据丢失，同步复制增强了分布式系统的整体韧性和可靠性。

Data durability

Synchronous replicas guarantee that data is durably stored across multiple replicas. When a write operation is confirmed by both the leader and the synchronous follower replicas, that ensures that the data is safely persisted on multiple machines. This redundancy provides data durability, protecting against data loss in the event of a replica failure or system crash. By maintaining multiple synchronized copies, synchronous replication ensures that critical data remains intact and recoverable, enhancing the overall data resilience of the system.

同步副本保证数据被持久存储在多个副本上。当写操作同时被 leader 和同步 follower 副本确认时，就确保数据已安全地持久化到多台机器上。这种冗余提供数据持久性，防止在副本故障或系统崩溃时数据丢失。通过维护多份同步拷贝，同步复制确保关键数据保持完整且可恢复，从而提升系统的整体数据韧性。

Consistency in read operations

Synchronous replication ensures consistency not only in write operations but also in read operations. As the synchronous replicas are always up to date with the leader, read operations can be performed on any of the replicas with the guarantee of accessing the most recent and consistent data. This feature enables load balancing and improves the system’s ability to handle read-intensive workloads.

同步复制不仅确保写操作的一致性，也确保读操作的一致性。由于同步副本始终与 leader 保持最新，可以在任意副本上执行读操作，并保证访问到最新、最一致的数据。这一特性支持负载均衡，并提升系统处理读密集型负载的能力。

In summary, synchronous replication in distributed databases provides the benefits of consistent writes, immediate failover, data durability, and consistency in read operations. By maintaining synchronous replicas that are always in sync with the leader, this replication mechanism ensures data integrity, continuous availability, and reliable

总之，分布式数据库中的同步复制提供一致写入、立即故障转移、数据持久性和读操作一致性等好处。通过维护始终与 leader 同步的副本，这种复制机制确保数据完整性、持续可用性以及可靠的

Page 83

access to up-to-date information. Synchronous replication is particularly valuable in scenarios where strict consistency and high availability are paramount, such as in financial systems, real-time applications, and mission-critical environments.

对最新信息的访问。在严格一致性和高可用至关重要的场景中（例如金融系统、实时应用和关键任务环境），同步复制尤其有价值。

Asynchronous replication

In distributed databases, asynchronous replication provides a mechanism for replicating data from a leader replica to asynchronous replicas. This replication approach has specific characteristics and considerations:

在分布式数据库中，异步复制提供一种把数据从 leader 副本复制到异步副本的机制。这种复制方式有其特定的特征和注意事项：

Near real-time updates

Asynchronous replicas apply changes from the leader replica in near real time, albeit with a potential delay. This means that the asynchronous replicas may not be immediately up to date with the latest changes made on the leader. The time lag between the leader and asynchronous replicas results in a temporary inconsistency in data across the replicas. However, over time, the asynchronous replicas converge as they catch up with the leader’s updates.

异步副本以近实时的方式应用来自 leader 副本的更改，但可能存在延迟。这意味着异步副本可能不会立即与 leader 上的最新更改保持同步。leader 与异步副本之间的时间差会导致副本间数据的暂时不一致。然而，随着时间推移，异步副本会追赶上 leader 的更新并最终收敛。

Data lag and potential staleness

Due to the asynchronous nature of replication, the asynchronous replicas can lag the leader replica. The extent of this lag depends on various factors, such as network conditions, system load, and the volume of changes being replicated. As a result, the asynchronous replicas may not reflect the most recent state of the data. This potential staleness can affect applications or use cases that require access to the most up-to-date information. It’s essential to consider this trade-off between near real-time updates and potential data lag when employing asynchronous replication.

由于复制的异步本质，异步副本可能落后于 leader 副本。这种滞后的程度取决于多种因素，例如网络状况、系统负载以及被复制更改的量。因此，异步副本可能无法反映数据的最新状态。这种潜在的陈旧性可能影响那些需要访问最新信息的应用或用例。在采用异步复制时，必须权衡近实时更新与潜在数据滞后之间的取舍。

Risk of data loss

Because asynchronous replicas can be lagging or stale, promoting an asynchronous replica as the new leader in the event of a leader-replica crash can introduce the risk of data loss. Since the asynchronous replica may not have received or applied all the changes made on the previous leader, promoting it prematurely can result in missing or inconsistent data. To mitigate this risk, careful considerations and measures, such as monitoring the replication lag and ensuring that the asynchronous replica has caught up sufficiently, should be taken before promoting it as the new leader.

由于异步副本可能滞后或陈旧，在 leader 副本崩溃时把一个异步副本提升为新 leader 可能引入数据丢失风险。因为异步副本可能尚未接收或应用前一个 leader 所做的全部更改，过早提升它会导致数据缺失或不一致。为缓解这一风险，在把它提升为新 leader 之前，应仔细考量并采取措施，例如监控复制延迟、确保异步副本已充分追平。

Scalability and performance

Asynchronous replication is often favored in distributed systems that prioritize scalability and performance over strict consistency. By allowing some flexibility in the replication process and tolerating temporary data inconsistencies, asynchronous replication can handle high write throughput and accommodate systems with large-scale deployments. This approach enables the system to distribute the workload and scale horizontally while maintaining acceptable response times.

在那些把可扩展性和性能置于严格一致性之上的分布式系统中，异步复制常受青睐。通过在复制过程中允许一定灵活性、容忍暂时的数据不一致，异步复制可以处理高写入吞吐，并容纳大规模部署的系统。这种方式让系统能够分布工作负载并水平扩展，同时保持可接受的响应时间。

Page 84

In summary, asynchronous replication in distributed databases provides near real-time updates but introduces the possibility of data lag and potential staleness. While it offers scalability and performance advantages, the risk of data loss exists when promoting an asynchronous replica as a new leader. Careful planning, monitoring, and appropriate fallback mechanisms are necessary to ensure data integrity and minimize the impact of data inconsistencies when employing asynchronous replication.

总之，分布式数据库中的异步复制提供近实时更新，但也引入了数据滞后和潜在陈旧的可能性。虽然它提供可扩展性和性能上的优势，但在把异步副本提升为新 leader 时存在数据丢失风险。在采用异步复制时，必须仔细规划、监控并配备适当的回退机制，以确保数据完整性并尽量减少数据不一致的影响。

Scaling distributed relational databases is an important task for businesses that need to handle increasing amounts of data and traffic. Partitioning, sharding, and replication are all useful techniques for scaling databases. Partitioning can improve query performance by reducing the amount of data that needs to be scanned to execute a query. Sharding is useful for scaling databases that have become too large to be managed on a single server. Replication is useful for scaling databases that require high availability or have heavy read traffic.

扩展分布式关系数据库是需要处理不断增长的数据和流量的企业的重要任务。分区、分片和复制都是扩展数据库的有用技术。分区可以通过减少执行查询所需扫描的数据量来提升查询性能。分片对于扩展那些已经大到无法在单台服务器上管理的数据库很有用。复制对于扩展那些要求高可用或读流量繁重的数据库很有用。

To conclude the chapter, let’s go over the most popular open source RDBMS choices.

作为本章收尾，我们来看看最流行的开源 RDBMS 选择。

Open Source Relational Database Systems

Open source RDBMSs are popular choices for businesses and developers because of their affordability, flexibility, and community support. Two widely used open source RDBMSs are MySQL and PostgreSQL. In this section, we will compare MySQL and PostgreSQL.

开源 RDBMS 因其经济、灵活和社区支持而成为企业和开发者的热门选择。两个被广泛使用的开源 RDBMS 是 MySQL 和 PostgreSQL。本节将比较 MySQL 和 PostgreSQL。

MySQL

MySQL is an open source RDBMS that was first released in 1995. It is one of the most popular RDBMSs in the world, with a large user community and a broad range of features. MySQL is known for its speed and scalability, making it an ideal choice for businesses that need to handle high volumes of data and traffic.

MySQL 是一个开源 RDBMS，首次发布于 1995 年。它是世界上最受欢迎的 RDBMS 之一，拥有庞大的用户社区和广泛的功能。MySQL 以其速度和可扩展性著称，使其成为需要处理海量数据和流量的企业的理想选择。

Features of MySQL include:

MySQL 的特性包括：

  • Support for SQL and NoSQL queries
    支持 SQL 和 NoSQL 查询
  • Scalable architecture
    可扩展的架构
  • High performance
    高性能
  • Simplicity and ease of use
    简单易用
  • Ability to handle read-heavy workloads
    处理读多写少负载的能力
  • Strong support for clustering and replication
    对集群和复制的强大支持

PostgreSQL

PostgreSQL is an open source RDBMS that was first released in 1996. It is known for its robustness, reliability, and feature-richness. PostgreSQL is a popular choice for

PostgreSQL 是一个开源 RDBMS，首次发布于 1996 年。它以健壮、可靠和功能丰富著称。PostgreSQL 是以下企业的流行选择：
